subject: english
question:
Choose the idiom/phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

She never has to worry about money as she is **born into a very rich family**.

options.text: Born with a silver spoon in mouth

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. Born with a silver spoon in mouth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Born with a silver spoon in mouth"** means to be born into a wealthy and privileged family. (अमीर परिवार में पैदा होना)

 
 
• **Example:** She never had to work hard for anything as she was born with a silver spoon in her mouth.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3 i.e. Born with a silver spoon in mouth**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Spill the beans** (राज़ खोल देना): To reveal secret information unintentionally or indiscreetly.

 
 
• **Example:** He accidentally spilled the beans about the surprise party.
 
 
 
• **Out of the blue** (अचानक से): Something happening unexpectedly and without any warning.
 
 
• **Example:** She called me out of the blue after years of no contact.
 
 
 
• **Eats like a bird** (बहुत कम खाना): To eat very little.
 
 
• **Example:** She eats like a bird and never finishes her meals.
